nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How many different purchasing situations were the participants presented with in the experiment?
nodes.answer: Participants were presented with 13 different purchasing situations where they were asked to estimate their likelihood of purchasing the product.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Minimalist lifestyles|Intentional purchasing_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: How do Liu, Lee, and Lien (2021) use the knowledge-attitude-behaviour (LAB) model and TPB to predict consumers' purchase intention for ethical fashion?
nodes.answer: They use the LAB model and TPB to predict consumers' purchase intention for ethical fashion based on their sensory perception and personality traits.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Minimalist lifestyles|Intentional purchasing_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of the extended theory of planned behaviour model in investigating the purchase intention of green products among Thai consumers as discussed by Manchu et al. (2016)?
nodes.answer: Manchu et al. (2016) highlight the importance of the extended theory of planned behaviour model in understanding the factors that influence Thai consumers' intention to purchase green products, such as attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioural control, and environmental concern.
